memory_candidates.content: When a shared bash-in-markdown skill file (e.g. skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md) needs a new conditional fork inserted into several near-identical existing dispatch handlers, the file's own convention of splitting a single logical if/else/fi across separate ```bash fenced blocks (interspersed with prose) means `bash -n` on any one fenced block in isolation will spuriously fail. Verify correctness instead by extracting just that handler's own bash blocks in document order and confirming the first line of each is exactly `if ...; then` / `else` / `fi` (or the nested equivalent) — i.e. verify block-sequence balance, not per-block syntax.

When a plan's Decision Record narrows a task's file_scope to an exact small set of files, verify the untouched-file guarantee at the end with `git diff <pre-task-sha>..HEAD --stat -- <broad-parent-dir>` rather than only `git status --short` on the specific excluded paths — the diff-stat form catches any file outside the declared scope that got modified, not just the specific files you remembered to check.
